h(du/s.head: ἡδύς
h(du/s.html: ἡδύς ἡδεῖα, ἡδύ. Also fem. ἡδύς Od. 12.369 [σϝαδ- as in ἁνδάνω.] 1 Sweet or pleasant. a To the taste. Of wine Od. 2.350, Od. 3.51, Od. 4.746, Od. 7.265, Od. 9.162, etc. Of a meal: δεῖπνον Od. 20.391. b To the sense of smell: ὀδμή Od. 9.210. Cf. Od. 12.369. c To the ear: ἀοιδήν Od. 8.64. 2 Of sleep or rest, sweet, grateful, balmy, refreshing Il. 4.131: Od. 1.364 = Od. 16.451 = Od. 19.604 = Od. 21.358, Od. 15.44, Od. 19.510, Od. 23.17. Superl. ἥδιστος: ὕπνος Od. 13.80. 3 Pleasing, agreeable, such as commends itself to one: εἴ πως τόδε πᾶσι φίλον καὶ ἡδὺ γένοιτο Il. 4.17. Cf. Il. 7.387: Od. 24.435. 4 In neut. ἡδύ as adv. a So as to gratify the sense of smell, sweetly: ἀμβροσίην ἡδὺ πνείουσαν Od. 4.446. b Of sleeping, sweetly: ἡδὺ κνώσσουσα Od. 4.809. c Of laughing, merrily, heartily: ἡδὺ γελάσσας Il. 11.378. Cf. Il. 2.270, Il. 21.508, Il. 23.784: = Od. 20.358 = Od. 21.376, Od. 16.354, Od. 18.35, 111.

h)nopi/dhs.head: Ἠνοπίδης
h)nopi/dhs.html: Ἠνοπίδης Patronymic from next. Of Satnius Il. 14.444 .

h)=qos.head: ἦθος
h)=qos.html: ἦθος τό [conn. with ἔθω and orig. σϝῆθος.] In pl., the accustomed haunts of animals: ἤθεα ἵππων Il. 6.511 = Il. 15.268. The sties of swine Od. 14.411.

h(ba/w.head: ἡβάω
h(ba/w.html: ἡβάω [ἥβη.] Acc. sing. masc. pres. pple. ἡβώοντα Il. 9.446. Nom. pl. ἡβώοντες Il. 24.604: Od. 10.6. Nom. fem. ἡβώωσα Od. 5.69. Opt. ἡβώοιμι Il. 7.157, Il. 11.670, Il. 23.629: Od. 14.468, 503. Contr. ἡβῷμι Il. 7.133. 3 sing. aor. subj. ἡβήσῃ Od. 1.41. Pple. ἡβήσας Od. 19.410. Dual masc. ἡβήσαντε Il. 5.550. 1 To be in one's youthful prime, in the vigour of early manhood: ἀνὴρ μάλʼ ἡβῶν Il. 12.382. Cf. Il. 7.133, 157 = Il. 11.670, Il. 9.446, Il. 23.629, Il. 24.565, 604: = Od. 10.6, Od. 14.468, 503, Od. 23.187. Of a flourishing vine Od. 5.69. 2 In aor., to have attained this stage of growth: ἡβήσαντε ἅμʼ Ἀργείοισιν ἑπέσθην Il. 5.550. Cf. Od. 1.41, Od. 19.410.

h(midah/s.head: ἡμιδαής
h(midah/s.html: ἡμιδαής [ἡμι- + δα(ϝ)-, δαίω1.] Half - burnt Il. 16.294.

h)io/eis.head: ἠϊόεις
h)io/eis.html: ἠϊόεις -εντος. Epithet of a river, of unknown meaning: ἐπʼ ἠϊόεντι σκαμάνδρῳ Il. 5.36.

h)iw/n.head: ἠϊών
h)iw/n.html: ἠϊών -όνος, ἡ. Dat. pl. ἠϊόνεσσι Od. 5.156. 1 A beach or shore of the sea: ἠϊόνος προπάροιθε βαθείης Il. 2.92. Cf. Il. 7.462, Il. 12.31, Il. 14.36, Il. 20.148, Il. 23.61. 2 In pl. a Portions of the shore, beaches, shores: ἀμφʼ ἄκραι ἠϊόνες βοόωσιν (to their furthest points) Il. 17.265 (v.l. ἄκραι ἠϊόνος, taking ἄκραι as sb. (see ἄκρη 3) and ἠϊόνος in sense (1), the headlands of the shore), ἠὼς φαινομένη ὑπεὶρ ἅλα τʼ ἠϊόνας τε Il. 24.13. Cf. Od. 5.156. b Beaches or spits projecting into the sea: ἠϊόνας παραπλῆγας Od. 5.418 = 440. Cf. Od. 6.138.

h)me/n.head: ἠμέν
h)me/n.html: ἠμέν [ἦ2 μέν.] Correlative with ἠδέ. ἠμὲν . . . ἠδὲ . . ., both . . . and . . .: ἠμὲν νέοι ἠδὲ γέροντες Il. 2.789. Cf. Il. 5.751, Il. 9.36, Il. 11.7, Il. 12.159, Il. 15.226, etc.: ἠμὲν ἀπείλησας . . . ἠδὲ . . . (you boasted that . . . and lo . . .) Od. 8.383. Cf. Od. 1.97, Od. 2.68, Od. 3.105, Od. 10.22, Od. 14.193, etc. So ἠμὲν . . . ἠδὲ . . . ἠδὲ . . . Il. 4.258, etc.– ἠμὲν . . . δὲ . . . Il. 12.428.– ἠμὲν . . . τε . . . Od. 8.575. Retaining something of the original emphasis (surely . . . and even so . . .) Il. 1.453, etc.

h)gere/qomai.head: ἠγερέθομαι
h)gere/qomai.html: ἠγερέθομαι [ἀγείρομαι. Cf. ἠερέθομαι beside ἀείρομαι.] 1 To come or gather together, assemble: ἀμφʼ Ἀτρεΐωνα ἠγερέθοντο Il. 23.233. Cf. Il. 2.304, Il. 10.127, Il. 19.303, Il. 24.783: περὶ ἑταῖροι ἠγερέθοντο Od. 2.392. Cf. Od. 3.412, Od. 11.228, Od. 17.34, 65, Od. 18.41, Od. 19.542, Od. 24.468. 2 To be or remain gathered together or in a body: ἀμφί μιν κρητῶν ἀγοὶ ἠγερέθονται Il. 3.231. Cf. Il. 12.82.

h)ero/fwnos.head: ἠερόφωνος
h)ero/fwnos.html: ἠερόφωνος [perh. fr. ἀείρω + φωνή. Cf. ἠερέθομαι, μετ-ήορος. Lifting up the voice.] Thus, loud-voiced. Epithet of heralds Il. 18.505.

h)ga/qeos.head: ἠγάθεος
h)ga/qeos.html: ἠγάθεος -η, -ον [app. ἠγα- = ἀγα- + θεῖος.] Holy, sacred. Like ζάθεος, epithet of placesIl. 1.252, Il. 2.722, Il. 6.133, Il. 21.58, 79: Od. 2.308, Od. 4.599, 702 = Od. 5.20, Od. 8.80, Od. 14.180.

h(/mwn.head: ἥμων
h(/mwn.html: ἥμων -ονος, ὁ [ἡ-, ἵημι1.] One skilled in throwing (the spear): ἥμονες ἄνδρες Il. 23.886.

h(=ma.head: ἧμα
h(=ma.html: ἧμα -ατος, τό [ἡ-, ἵημι1.] A throwing or hurling. In pl.: ὅσσον ἥμασιν ἔπλευ ἄριστος (in throwing the spear) Il. 23.891.

h(=xi.head: ἧχι
h(=xi.html: ἧχι [ᾗ (see ὅς2 II.6) + advbl. suff. -χι.] Where: ἡ. ἑκάστῳ δῶμα Ἥφαιστος ποίησεν Il. 1.607. Cf. Il. 3.326, Il. 5.774, Il. 8.14, Il. 11.76: Od. 3.292, Od. 6.94, Od. 19.553. In an object clause: ἄλλους πευθόμεθʼ, ἡ. ἕκαστος ἀπώλετο Od. 3.87.

h)eroeidh/s.head: ἠεροειδής
h)eroeidh/s.html: ἠεροειδής -ές [ἠερ-, ἀήρ + εἶδος.] 1 Epithet of the sea, misty, melting into the haze of distance Il. 23.744: Od. 2.263, Od. 3.105, 294, Od. 4.482, Od. 5.164, 281, Od. 8.568 = Od. 13.150 = 176, Od. 12.285. In neut. ἠεροειδές as adv., through the haze, in the haze of distance: ὅσσον ἠ. ἀνὴρ ἴδεν Il. 5.770. 2 Of a rock, shrouded in mist Od. 12.233 (cf. 74). 3 Epithet of caves, dim, dusky, shadowy Od. 12.80, Od. 13.103 = 347, 366.

h)ioneu/s.head: Ἠϊονεύς-1
h)ioneu/s.html:
Ἠϊονεύς-1 Greek. Killed by Hector Il. 7.11 .
Ἠϊονεύς-2. Father of Rhesus-1 Il. 10.435.

h)=tor.head: ἦτορ
h)=tor.html: ἦτορ τό. Only in nom. and acc. sing. 1 The heart: πάλλεται ἠ. ἀνὰ στόμα Il. 22.452. Cf. Il. 10.93. 2 The heart, breast, soul, mind. As the seat or a seat a α Of life, vitality, the vital powers, strength (cf. θυμός I 1.a): εἰ χάλκεόν μοι ἠ. ἐνείη Il. 2.490: τετιημένος ἠ. Od. 7.287. Cf. Od. 4.703 = Od. 23.205, Od. 19.136, Od. 24.345. Hence β The animating principle, the vital spirit, the soul, the life, life, one's life (cf. θυμός I.1.b): μὴ ἠ. ὀλέσσῃς Il. 5.250. Cf. Il. 11.115 (of fawns), Il. 15.252, Il. 16.660, Il. 17.535, Il. 21.201, Il. 24.50: ἀπορραῖσαι ἠ. Od. 16.428. b Of spirit, courage, stoutness, resolution, endurance: ἄλκιμον ἠ. Il. 5.529. Cf. Il. 3.31, Il. 16.209, 242, 264 (of wasps), Il. 17.111 (of a lion), Il. 19.169, Il. 20.169 (of a lion), Il. 21.114, 425, 571, Il. 24.205, 521: μινύθει τοι ἠ. ἐταίρων Od. 4.374. Cf. Od. 4.467, 481 = Od. 10.496, Od. 5.297 = 406 = Od. 22.147, Od. 9.256, Od. 10.198 = 566 = Od. 12.277, Od. 22.68. c Of anger, wrath, passion: κεχολωμένος ἠ. (in his heart) Il. 14.367. Cf. Il. 10.107, Il. 24.585. d Of desire or appetite: σίτοιο ἄσασθαι ἠ. Il. 19.307. e Of volition: τίς σφῶϊν μαίνεται ἠ.; Il. 8.413. Cf. Il. 15.166, 182: δῶρον ὅττι κέ μοι δοῦναι ἠ. ἀνώγῃ Od. 1.316. f Of feelings, emotions, moods: τετιημέναι ἠ. Il. 8.437, χαίρει μοι ἠ. Il. 23.647. Cf. Il. 5.364, 670, Il. 9.9, 705, Il. 10.575 (their tired hearts), Il. 11.556, Il. 13.84, Il. 15.554, Il. 16.450, 509, Il. 19.366, Il. 21.389, Il. 22.169: ἠ. οἱ ἰάνθη Od. 4.840, τάφος οἱ ἠ. ἵκανεν Od. 23.93. Cf. Od. 1.48, 60, 114, Od. 2.298, Od. 4.538, 804, Od. 7.269, Od. 8.303, Od. 9.62 = 105 = 565 = Od. 10.77 = 133, Od. 10.313, Od. 13.286, 320, Od. 15.481, Od. 16.92, Od. 17.46, 514, Od. 18.153, Od. 20.22, 84, Od. 23.53. g Of the faculty of deliberating or considering: ἠ οἱ μερμήριξεν Il. 1.188. Of recollection: ὥς μοι ἰνδάλλεται ἠ. Od. 19.224.– h Of one's character or dispostion: ἀμείλιχον ἠ. ἔχουσα Il. 9.572. Cf. Il. 9.497: Od. 23.172.

h)erofoi=tis.head: ἠεροφοῖτις
h)erofoi=tis.html: ἠεροφοῖτις [ἠερ-, ἀήρ + φοιτάω.] Walking in darkness. Epithet of Erinys Il. 9.571, Il. 19.87.

h)leo/s.head: ἠλεός
h)leo/s.html: ἠλεός [app. conn. with ἀλάομαι, ἠλάσκω.] Voc. ἠλέ Il. 15.128. 1 Crazed, distraught: φρένας ἠλέ (in your . . .) Il. 15.128. Cf. Od. 2.243. 2 That takes away one's wits or discretion: οἶνος Od. 14.464.

h)=ka.head: ἦκα
h)=ka.html: ἦκα 1 Of action, gently, without effort: ψύξασα Il. 20.440. Cf. Il. 23.336: Od. 18.92, 94, Od. 20.301. Gently, without violence: ἀπώσατο γέροντα Il. 24.508. 2 Of journeying, softly, at a foot-pace Od. 17.254. 3 Of speaking, softly, in an undertone Il. 3.155. 4 Of the soft play of light on a glossy surface: χιτῶνας ἦκα στίλβοντας ἐλαίῳ Il. 18.596.

h)i/qeos.head: ἠΐθεος
h)i/qeos.html: ἠΐθεος -ου, ὁ. An unmarried youth Il. 4.474, Il. 11.60, Il. 18.567, 593, Il. 22.127, 128: Od. 3.401, Od. 6.63, Od. 11.38.

h(gemw/n.head: ἡγεμών
h(gemw/n.html: ἡγεμών -όνος, ὁ [ἡγέομαι.] 1 A guide or pilot, one who shows the way: ἅμʼ ἡγεμόνʼ ἐσθλὸν ὄπασσον Od. 15.310. Cf. Od. 10.505. 2 A leader, commander or chief: κέλευεν οἷσιν ἕκαστος ἡγεμόνων Il. 4.429. Cf. Il. 2.365, Il. 3.1, Il. 5.38, Il. 9.85, Il. 12.87, etc.

h)laska/zw.head: ἠλασκάζω
h)laska/zw.html: ἠλασκάζω [cf. ἠλάσκω.] 1 To wander aimlessly about Il. 18.281. 2 To go about or skulk in order to avoid (danger): ὅππῃ ἐμὸν μένος ἠλασκάζει Od. 9.457.

h)/ios.head: ἤϊος
h)/ios.html: ἤϊος Epithet of Apollo, of unknown meaning: ἤϊε Φοῖβε Il. 15.365, Il. 20.152.

h(/rh.head: Ἥρη
h(/rh.html: Ἥρη (Ἀργείη, βοῶπις, Διὸς κυδρὴ παράκοιτις, ἠΰκομος , θεά, λευκώλενος, πότνια, πρέσβα θεά, χρυσόθρονος, χρυσοπέδιλος ). Daughter of Cronus and Rhea, sister of Zeus , Hades, Poseidon and Demeter, and wife (and sister) of Zeus. For her children see under Ζεύς. Reared by Oceanus and Tethys Il. 14.200, 302. She suspects the promise of Zeus to Thetis Il. 1.536; reproaches Zeus for favouring the Trojans Il. 4.20, they come to terms 31; she urges Athene to the fray Il. 5.711, prepares a chariot 720, consults Zeus 753, conveys Athene to the field 767; urges Athene again to the field Il. 8.350, they are stopped by Iris sent by Zeus 413; arrays herself to beguile Zeus Il. 14.166, gets the aid of Aphrodite 188, and of Sleep 231, the beguilement 292, Zeus wakens Il. 15.4 , and sends her to summon Iris and Apollo 54; how she tricked Zeus in the matter of the birth of Heracles Il. 19.95; summons Hephaestus to quell Xanthus-1 Il. 21.328 ; in the Battle of the Gods assaults Artemis Il. 21.489; etc. : Od. 4.513, Od. 8.465 , Od. 11.604, Od. 12.72, Od. 15.112, 180, Od. 20.70.

h(nioxeu/w.head: ἡνιοχεύω
h(nioxeu/w.html: ἡνιοχεύω [ἡνίοχος.] 1 To act as ἡνίοχος of a war-chariot, drive it Il. 11.103, Il. 23.641, 642. 2 To drive a waggon Od. 6.319.

h)/n.head: ἤν
h)/n.html: ἤν [εἰ ἄν.] With subj. 1 Introducing in protasis one of two opposed clauses, even if, even though, though, granted that = εἰ 4. For the examples see (II) of Table at end. 2 Introducing the protasis of conditional sentences, if, on condition that, supposing that = εἰ 5. For the examples see (III) of Table. 3 In final clauses, if haply, in the hope that = εἰ 9..b: ἐμὲ πρόες, ἤν πού τι φόως Δαναοῖσι γένωμαι Il. 16.39. Cf. Il. 7.39, Il. 14.78, Il. 17.245, Il. 20.172, Il. 22.419: ἤν που ἀκούσῃ (ἀκούσω) Od. 1.94, Od. 2.360, Od. 3.83. Cf. Od. 1.282, Od. 2.216, Od. 5.417. 4 In an object clause, whether = εἰ 10 b : ὄφρα ἴδῃ ἤν τοι χραίσμῃ φιλότης Il. 15.32.

h)/peiros.head: ἤπειρος
h)/peiros.html: ἤπειρος -ου, ἡ. 1 The land as opposed to the sea: νῆʼ ἐπʼ ἠπείροιο ἔρυσσαν Il. 1.485: εἴτʼ ἐπʼ ἠπείρου . . . εἴτʼ ἐν πελάγει Od. 3.90. Cf. Od. 1.162, Od. 5.348, 350, 399, 402, Od. 9.85 = Od. 10.56, Od. 9.496, Od. 13.114, Od. 14.136, Od. 16.325, 359, 367. 2 Inland parts as opposed to the coast Od. 9.49. 3 The mainland, as opposed to an island or islands: οἳ ἤπειρον ἕχον Il. 2.635 (the coast of the mainland opposite the islands): οὔτʼ ἠπείροιο οὔτʼ αὐτῆς Ἰθάκης Od. 14.97. Cf. Od. 13.235, Od. 14.100, Od. 21.109, Od. 24.378.

h(=los.head: ἧλος
h(=los.html: ἧλος -ου, ὁ [ϝῆλος. Cf. L. vallus.] A nail or stud used for ornament Il. 1.246, Il. 11.29, 633.

h(mitelh/s.head: ἡμιτελής
h(mitelh/s.html: ἡμιτελής [ἡμι- + τελέω.] Half-finished, half-built: δόμος Il. 2.701.

h)maqo/eis.head: ἠμαθόεις
h)maqo/eis.html: ἠμαθόεις -εντος [ἄμαθος.] Abounding in sand, sandy, by the sandy shore. Epithet of Pylus Il. 2.77, Il. 9.153 = 295, Il. 11.712: Od. 1.93, Od. 2.214 = 359, Od. 2.326, Od. 4.633, Od. 11.257, 459, Od. 24.152.

h)laka/th.head: ἠλακάτη
h)laka/th.html: ἠλακάτη -ης, ἡ. A distaff Il. 6.491: = Od. 1.357 = Od. 21.351, Od. 4.131, 135.

h(gemoneu/w.head: ἡγεμονεύω
h(gemoneu/w.html: ἡγεμονεύω [ἡγεμών.] 1 To act as guide or pilot, show the way: θεός τις ἡγεμόνευεν Od. 9.142, Od. 10.141. Cf. Od. 17.194. With dat., to guide (a person), show (him) the way: δεῦρό οἱ ἡγεμόνευεν Od. 17.372. Cf. Od. 10.445. With cognate acc., to show (the way): ὁδὸν ἡγεμονεύσω Od. 6.261, Od. 7.30. Cf. Od. 10.501. 2 To lead the way, act as leader, take the lead: Τηλέμαχος πρόσθʼ ἡγεμόνευεν Od. 22.400. With dat.: τοῖσιν ἡγεμόνευεν Od. 3.386, Od. 8.4 = 421, Od. 23.293. With dat. and cognate acc.: τοῖσιν ὁδὸν ἡγεμόνευεν Od. 24.225. Sim.: ὅτʼ ἀνὴρ ὀχετηγὸς ὕδατι ῥόον ἡγεμονεύῃ (guides the flow) Il. 21.258. 3 To lead the way, give a lead, in a course of action: τῇ ἴμεν ᾗ κε σὺ ἡγεμονεύῃς Il. 15.46. 4 To precede a person by an interval of time: Ὀδυσσεὺς ὕστερος, αὐτὰρ Τηλέμαχος πρόσθʼ ἡγεμόνευεν Od. 24.155. 5 To be the leader, commander or chief of. a With genit.: λοκρῶν Il. 2.527, τῆς ἑτέρης [στιχός] Il. 16.179. Cf. Il. 2.540, 552, 645, 657, etc. b With dat.: Τρωσίν Il. 2.816. 6 Absol., to act as chief or leader, lead one's men Il. 13.53, Il. 16.92.

h(gh/twr.head: ἡγήτωρ
h(gh/twr.html: ἡγήτωρ -ορος, ὁ [ἡγέομαι.] A leader, commander or chief: δύω ἡγήτορες ἦσαν Il. 4.393. Cf. Il. 2.79, Il. 3.153, Il. 10.181, Il. 15.330, Il. 20.383, etc.: Ταφίων Od. 1.105. Cf. Od. 7.98, 136, 186 = Od. 8.26 = 97 = 387 = 536, Od. 8.11, Od. 11.526, Od. 13.186, 210. With ἀνήρ: Πυλίων ἡγήτορες ἄνδρες Il. 11.687. Cf. Il. 16.495, 532.

h)pedano/s.head: ἠπεδανός
h)pedano/s.html: ἠπεδανός [prob. for ἀ-πεδ-ανός fr. ἀ-1 + πεδ-, ποδ-, πούς. Not firm on the feet. Cf. ἔμπεδος.] Thus, weakly, feeble Il. 8.104: Od. 8.311.

h)lito/mhnos.head: ἠλιτόμηνος
h)lito/mhnos.html: ἠλιτόμηνος [ἀλιτ-, ἀλιταίνω + μήν. Failing in (the due number of) months.] Untimely born Il. 19.118.

h(/domai.head: †ἥδομαι
h(/domai.html: †ἥδομαι [ἡδύς.] 3 sing. aor. ἥσατο Od. 9.353. Aor. pple. ἄσμενος, -ου Il. 14.108, Il. 20.350: Od. 9.63, 566, Od. 10.134. 1 In aor., to conceive delight or pleasure. With pple., expressing the occasion: ἥσατο πίνων Od. 9.353. 2 In aor. pple., having conceived or conceiving pleasure, well-pleased, glad: ἐμοί κεν ἀσμένῳ εἴη (I should be glad . . .) Il. 14.108, φύγεν ἄσμενος ἐκ θανάτοιο (was glad to flee . . .) Il. 20.350: προτέρω πλέομεν ἄσμενοι ἐκ θανάτοιο (glad to have escaped . . .) Od. 9.63 = Od. 9.566 = Od. 10.134.

h(/sswn.head: ἥσσων
h(/sswn.html: ἥσσων -ονος [for ἡκιων. Comp. fr. ἦκα. Cf. ἤκιστος.] 1 Of less worth or merit, inferior Il. 16.722, Il. 23.322, 858. 2 In neut. ἧσσον as adv., less: ὀλίγον τί μʼ ἡ. ἐτίμα Od. 15.365.

h)pu/w.head: ἠπύω
h)pu/w.html: ἠπύω (ἐπ-.) 1 To call to (a person): κύκλωπας Od. 9.399. Cf. Od. 10.83. 2 Of the wind, to roar Il. 14.399. Of the lyre, to sound Od. 17.271.

h)puti/dhs.head: Ἠπυτίδης
h)puti/dhs.html: Ἠπυτίδης Patronymic of Periphas-2 Il. 17.324.

h(ni/a.head: ἡνία
h(ni/a.html: ἡνία τά. The reins used in driving a chariot Il. 3.261, Il. 5.226, 262, 365, Il. 8.121, Il. 16.404, Il. 17.619, Il. 23.337, etc.: Od. 3.483, Od. 6.81.

h)/pios.head: ἤπιος
h)/pios.html: ἤπιος -η, -ον. 1 Well or kindly disposed, kindly, gentle, mild, not harsh or rigorous: ἤπια δήνεα οἶδεν (is well disposed towards me) Il. 4.361 (see εἴδω III.12), ἐθέλω τοι ἠ. εἶναι Il. 8.40 = Il. 22.184. Cf. Il. 24.770, 775: Od. 2.47, 230 = Od. 5.8, Od. 2.234 = Od. 5.12, Od. 10.337, Od. 11.441, Od. 13.314, Od. 14.139, Od. 15.152, 490. Absol. in neut. pl.: εἴ μοι ἤπια εἰδείη (were well disposed towards me) Il. 16.73: ὁμῶς τοι ἤπια οἶδεν (is at one with you in loyalty of heart) Od. 13.405 = Od. 15.39, ἀνάκτεσιν ἤπια εἰδώς (loyal to them) Od. 15.557. See in reference to these εἴδω III.12. 2 Giving kindly tendance, solicitous for the well-being of what is committed to one Il. 23.281. 3 Of speech, tending to effect reconcilement or bring peace Od. 20.327. 4 Of medicinal applications, soothing, allaying pain Il. 4.218, Il. 11.515, 830.

h)eri/boia.head: Ἠερίβοια
h)eri/boia.html: Ἠερίβοια (περικαλλής). Stepmother of (apparently) Otus-1 and Ephialtes. Her rescue of Ares Il. 5.389.

h(dueph/s.head: ἡδυεπής
h(dueph/s.html: ἡδυεπής [ἡδύς + ἔπος.] Sweet-speaking, silvertongued. Of Nestor Il. 1.248.

h)rige/neia.head: ἠριγένεια
h)rige/neia.html: ἠριγένεια -ης [ἦρι + γεν-, γίγνομαι.] Early-born. Epithet of Ἠώς Il. 8.508, Il. 1.477 = Il. 24.788: = Od. 2.1 = Od. 3.404 = 491 = Od. 4.306 = 431 = 576 = Od. 5.228 = Od. 8.1 = Od. 9.152 = 170 = 307 = 437 = 560 = Od. 10.187 = Od. 12.8 = 316 = Od. 13.18 = Od. 15.189 = Od. 17.1 = Od. 19.428, Od. 4.195, Od. 12.3, Od. 13.94. Without Ἠώς, the dawn: οὐδὲ σέ γʼ ἠ. λήσει Od. 22.197. Cf. Od. 23.347.

h(mi/qeos.head: ἡμίθεος
h(mi/qeos.html: ἡμίθεος [ἡμι- + θεός.] Half-divine, of divine parentage on one side: ἀνδρῶν Il. 12.23.

h(mita/lanton.head: ἡμιτάλαντον
h(mita/lanton.html: ἡμιτάλαντον τό [ἡμι- + τάλαντον.] A halftalent: χρυσοῦ Il. 23.751, 796.

h(/meros.head: ἥμερος
h(/meros.html: ἥμερος -ον. Tame, domestic: χῆνα Od. 15.162.

h(ni/oxos.head: ἡνίοχος
h(ni/oxos.html: ἡνίοχος -ου, ὁ [ἡνία + ὀχ-, ἔχω. He that holds the reins.] 1 The driver of a war-chariot as distinguished from the παραιβάτης or fighting man: παραιβάται ἡνίοχοί τε Il. 23.132. Cf. Il. 5.231, 580, Il. 8.119, 124 = 316, Il. 8.126, Il. 11.47 = Il. 12.84, Il. 11.161, 273 = 399, Il. 11.280, Il. 12.111, Il. 13.386, 394, 537 = Il. 14.431, Il. 17.427, 439, 610, Il. 18.225, Il. 23.280. 2 Used loosely of the παραιβάτης (cf. ἡνιοχεύς 2): θρασὺν ἡνίοχον φορέοντες Ἕκτορα Il. 8.89 (Eniopeus was driving, see 119, where he also is called ἡ.). In pl. including both the ἡ. proper and the παραιβάτης: σὺν ἡνιόχοισι κακοῖσιν Il. 17.487. 3 One who drives his chariot in a race: μήτι ἡ. περιγίγνεται ἡνιόχοιο Il. 23.318. Cf. Il. 23.460, 465, 502.

h)e/rios.head: ἠέριος
h)e/rios.html: ἠέριος -η (ἠϝέριος) [ἀϝερ-. Cf. ἠώς, ἄριστον, αὔριον, ἦρι, λ. aurora.] With the early morning: ἠερίη ἀνέβη οὐρανόν Il. 1.497. Cf. Il. 1.557, Il. 3.7: Od. 9.52.

h)li/batos.head: ἠλίβατος
h)li/batos.html: ἠλίβατος -ον. Of unknown meaning. Epithet of πέτρη Il. 15.273, 619, Il. 16.35: Od. 9.243, Od. 10.88, Od. 13.196.

h)w/s.head: ἠώς
h)w/s.html:
ἠώς -οῦς, ἡ (ἠϝώς) [ἀϝοσ-. Cf. ἠέριος.] Dat. ἠοῖ (ἠόι)̈ Il. 7.331, Il. 11.685, Il. 13.794, Il. 24.600, etc.: Od. 4.407, Od. 12.24, Od. 14.266, Od. 16.2, etc. Acc. ἠῶ (ἠόα) Il. 5.267, Il. 8.565, Il. 9.240, Il. 18.255, etc.: Od. 2.434, Od. 7.288, Od. 16.368, Od. 23.243, etc. Locative ἠῶθι Il. 11.50: Od. 5.469, Od. 6.36. 1 Dawn, the dawn, the daybreak: ἅμʼ ἠοῖ Il. 7.331, Il. 9.618, 682, Il. 11.685, Il. 24.600, ὅσον τʼ ἐπικίδναται ἠ. Il. 7.451, 458, ἠῶθι πρό (in front of the dawn, with the dawn) Il. 11.50: Od. 5.469, Od. 6.36. Cf. Il. 5.267, Il. 7.433, Il. 8.1, 508, Il. 10.251, Il. 23.227, Il. 24.12, 695: Od. 4.194, 407, Od. 6.31, Od. 7.222, Od. 12.24, Od. 14.266 = Od. 17.435, Od. 15.50, 396, Od. 16.2, 270. 2 A dawning or morning considered as a space of time: ὄφρʼ ἠ. ἦν Il. 8.66 = Il. 11.84, ἠοῦς ὄψεαι (in the morning) Il. 8.470, τὸν [μῦθον] ἠοῦς (the morrow's) 525. Cf. Il. 21.111: νηῦς ἠῶ πεῖρε κέλευθον (through the morning) Od. 2.434. Cf. Od. 7.288, Od. 9.56. 3 A morning considered as a point or unit of time or as one of a series: δυωδεκάτη Il. 1.493 = Il. 24.31, Il. 21.80, Il. 24.413. Cf. Il. 13.794, Il. 21.156, Il. 24.781, 785: Od. 19.192, 571. 4 The quarter of the dawn, the east: πρὸς ἠῶ τʼ ἠέλιόν τε Il. 12.239: Od. 9.26, Od. 13.240. Cf. Od. 10.190. 5 The dawn personified: ῥοδοδάκτυλος Ἠ. Il. 1.477 = Il. 24.788, Il. 6.175, Il. 9.707, Il. 23.109, Ἠ. ἐκ λεχέων ὄρνυτο Il. 11.1. Cf. Il. 2.48, Il. 8.565, Il. 9.240, 662, Il. 11.723, Il. 18.255, Il. 19.1, Il. 24.417: Ἠοῦς υἱός Od. 4.188. Cf. Od. 2.1, Od. 5.1, 121, 390, Od. 6.48, Od. 9.151, Od. 10.541, Od. 12.3, Od. 23.243, etc.
Ἠώς (δῖα, ἐΰθρονος, ἐϋπλόκαμος, ἠριγένεια, κροκόπεπλος, ῥοδοδάκτυλος , χρυσόθρονος). The Dawn. Wife of Tithonus and mother of Memnon. Carried off Orion Od. 5.121, and Cleitus-2 Od. 15.250. See also ἠώς 5 in Lexicon.

h(/misus.head: ἥμισυς
h(/misus.html: ἥμισυς -υ [ἡμι-.] 1 Half, half of: ἡμίσεες λαοί Od. 3.155. 2 Absol., half of what is specified or indicated. a ἡμίσεες εἰλεῦντο Il. 21.7. Cf. Od. 3.157, Od. 24.464. b In neut. ἥμισυ: τιμῆς ἡ. Il. 6.193. Cf. Il. 9.580 (following τὸ ἡ. 579 (see below)), Il. 17.231 (twice): Od. 9.246 (twice), Od. 13.114, Od. 17.322. With the article: τὸ δʼ ἡ. κεῖτʼ ἐπὶ γαίης Il. 13.565. Cf. Il. 9.579 3 In neut. as adv., to the extent of a half: ἡ. μείρεο τιμῆς Il. 9.616.

h(me/teros.head: ἡμέτερος
h(me/teros.html: ἡμέτερος -η, -ον [ἡμεῖς.] 1 Our Il. 2.374, Il. 3.233, Il. 6.58, Il. 10.342, Il. 11.720, etc.: Od. 1.45, Od. 2.26, Od. 6.191, Od. 11.33, Od. 13.181, etc. With the article: αἱ ἡμέτεραι ἄλοχοι Il. 2.136. Absol.: εἰς ἡμέτερον (sc. δῶμα) Od. 2.55 = Od. 17.534.–ἐφʼ ἡμέτερα (sc. δώματα) (to our homes, home) Il. 9.619. 2 My Il. 1.30, Il. 6.151 = Il. 20.214, Il. 7.363, Il. 9.108, Il. 15.224, Il. 16.244, Il. 19.73, Il. 21.60, Il. 24.567: Od. 1.397, Od. 3.186, Od. 4.101, Od. 8.255, Od. 10.334, Od. 11.562, Od. 16.45, 117, 300, 442, Od. 19.344, Od. 21.375, Od. 22.464, Od. 24.216. Absol.: ἐς ἡμέτερον (sc. δῶμα) Od. 7.301.–ἐφʼ ἡμέτερα (sc. δώματα) (home) Od. 15.88. (Sometimes, esp. in uses with οἶκος and the like, it is difficult to say which sense should be preferred.)

h)xh/.head: ἠχή
h)xh/.html: ἠχή -ῆς, (ϝηχή) [cf. (ϝ)ι(ϝ)άχω, (ϝ)ι(ϝ)αχή.] Sound, noise: ἠχῇ θεσπεσίῃ Il. 8.159 = Il. 15.590, Il. 12.252, Il. 13.834, Il. 15.355, Il. 16.769, Il. 23.213: Od. 3.150, Od. 11.633. Cf. Il. 2.209, Il. 13.837.

h(=mai.head: †ἧμαι
h(=mai.html: †ἧμαι [ἡσ-.] 1 sing. pres. ἧμαι Il. 18.104, Il. 24.542: Od. 8.157, Od. 14.41. 2 sing. ἧσαι Il. 2.255, Il. 15.245. 3 sing. ἧσται Il. 19.345: Od. 6.305, Od. 11.142, Od. 16.145, Od. 18.240, etc. 1 pl. ἥμεθα Il. 15.740. 2 pl. ἧσθε Od. 2.240. 3 pl. ἥαται (ἥσ-αται), also writtenεἵαται Il. 2.137, Il. 10.100, 161, 422: Od. 2.403, Od. 6.307. ἕαται Il. 3.134, Il. 9.628. 1 sing. impf. ἥμην Il. 6.336: Od. 10.374, Od. 11.49. 3 sing. ἧστο Il. 1.512, Il. 6.324, Il. 13.11, Il. 15.393, Il. 23.451, etc.: Od. 1.114, Od. 3.32, Od. 6.52, Od. 17.68, Od. 23.91, etc. 3 dual ἥσθην Il. 4.21, Il. 8.445, 458: Od. 7.232. 1 pl. ἥμεθα Od. 3.263, Od. 9.78, 162, Od. 11.10, 82, Od. 23.42, etc. 3 pl. ἥατο (ἥσ-ατο), also writtenεἵατο Il. 3.149, Il. 7.61, Il. 8.554, Il. 15.10, Il. 18.504, Il. 24.99, etc.: Od. 1.326, Od. 2.398, Od. 3.8, Od. 9.545, Od. 20.106, etc. ἕατο Il. 7.414. ἧντο Il. 3.153. Imp. ἧσο Il. 2.200, Il. 3.406, Il. 4.412: Od. 16.44, Od. 18.105, Od. 20.262. Pple. ἥμενος, -η Il. 1.330, 358, Il. 5.771, Il. 7.100, Il. 15.153, Il. 21.389, etc.: Od. 1.108, Od. 4.596, Od. 7.106, Od. 9.8, Od. 10.375, Od. 17.506, Od. 21.100, etc. Infin. ἧσθαι Il. 1.134, 416, Il. 13.253, 280: Od. 7.160, Od. 10.507, 536, Od. 19.120, Od. 23.365. (ἀφ-, ἐν-, ἐφ-, καθ-, μεθ-, παρ-.) 1 To sit, be seated: παρὰ κλισίῃ ἥμενον Il. 1.330, ἕαται σιγῇ Il. 3.134. Cf. Il. 2.200, Il. 4.21, Il. 6.324, Il. 8.445, Il. 9.190, Il. 13.11, etc.: ἥμενοι ἐν ῥινοῖσιν Od. 1.108. Cf. Od. 1.114, Od. 2.36, Od. 3.8, 32, Od. 6.52, Od. 8.157, Od. 10.374, etc. 2 To sit idle, doing nothing: ἥμενοι αὖθι ἕκαστοι ἀκήριοι Il. 7.100. Cf. Il. 1.134, Il. 13.253: οἶον ἧσθʼ ἄνεθͅ Od. 2.240. Cf. Od. 10.375, Od. 16.145. Requiring to do nothing: ἱστία ἐρύσαντες ἥμεθα Od. 9.78 = Od. 14.256. Cf. Od. 10.507, Od. 11.10 = Od. 12.152. 3 To sit, abide, be, remain, doing something specified or in a specified condition or place: ἀδάκρυτος ἧσθαι Il. 1.416, ἥαται ποτιδέγμεναι Il. 2.137, τηλόθι πάτρης ἧμαι ἐνὶ Τροίῃ Il. 24.542. Cf. Il. 2.255, Il. 4.412, Il. 8.480, Il. 9.628, Il. 10.100, 161, 422, Il. 15.740, Il. 18.104: Od. 3.263, Od. 13.337, 424, Od. 14.41, Od. 19.120, Od. 21.425. 4 Of an army, to be set down or encamped: τὴν πόλιν ἀμφὶ δύω στρατοὶ ἥατο Il. 18.509. Of a sentinel or scout, to be at his post Il. 10.182. To be posted: δύω σκοποὶ ἥατο Il. 18.523. Cf. Il. 24.799. 5 Of a thing, to be set, fixed, placed: ἔνθα μύλαι ἥατο Od. 20.106.

h(mipe/lekkon.head: ἡμιπέλεκκον
h(mipe/lekkon.html: ἡμιπέλεκκον -ου, τό [ἡμι- + πέλεκκον in sense axe.] A half-axe, an axe with a single cutting edge Il. 23.851, 858, 883.

h)mi/.head: †ἠμί
h)mi/.html: †ἠμί Only in 3 sing. impf. ἦ. To utter speech, speak, say: ἦ καὶ . . . Il. 1.219. Cf. Il. 1.528, Il. 3.292, 310, 355, etc.: Od. 2.321, Od. 3.337, Od. 6.198, Od. 9.371, etc.

h)de/.head: ἠδέ
h)de/.html: ἠδέ [ἦ2δέ.] And: ταύρων ἠδʼ αἰγῶν Il. 1.41. Cf. Il. 1.96, 251, Il. 2.27, 79, 118, etc.: Od. 1.13, 95, 135, 170, 182, 231, etc. So ἠδὲ καί: Διὸς ἄγγελοι ἠδὲ καὶ ἀνδρῶν Il. 1.334, etc. Cf. Od. 2.209, etc. Correlative with ἠμέν. See ἠμέν.

h(su/xios.head: ἡσύχιος
h(su/xios.html: ἡσύχιος At peace, undisturbed Il. 21.598.

h)niopeu/s.head: Ἠνιοπεύς
h)niopeu/s.html: Ἠνιοπεύς Son of Thebaeus-1. Chariot-driver to Hector. Killed by Diomedes Il. 8.120.

h)=.head: ἦ1
h)=.html:
ἦ1, 3 sing. impf. ἠμί.
ἦ2. 1 Affirmative or emphasizing particle a ἦ μέγα πένθος Ἀχαιΐδα γαῖαν ἱκάνει Il. 1.254. Cf. Il. 1.78, 232, 240, 255, 293, 342, etc.: ἦ μάλα δή σε διδάσκουσιν θεοὶ αὐτοί Od. 1.384. Cf. Od. 2.60, Od. 4.81, 663, 770, Od. 6.278, Od. 10.465, etc. With an ironical tone Il. 1.229: Od. 2.325. With concessive force, it is sure that, yet, although: ἦ καὶ γένει ὕστερος ἦεν Il. 3.215. b Combined with other particles α ἦ μάν Il. 2.370, Il. 13.354, etc. β ἦ μέν Il. 3.430, Il. 5.197, Il. 9.57 (yet to be sure you are young (heightening the preceding qualified praise)), etc.: Od. 10.65, Od. 11.447, Od. 13.425, etc. This combination introducing an oath Il. 1.77, Il. 14.275, Il. 19.109, etc.: Od. 14.160 = Od. 19.305.– ἦ μήν: ἦ μὴν Τρῶές γε κέλονται (I assure you, virtually = although) Il. 7.393. Cf. Il. 2.291. γ ἦ τε Il. 3.56, 366, Il. 5.201, Il. 10.450, etc.: Od. 1.288, Od. 2.62, Od. 12.138, etc. δ ἦ τοι (ἤτοι) Il. 1.68, 140, 211, Il. 2.813, etc.: Od. 1.155, 267, 307, 394, etc. 2 Interrogative particle a Introducing a direct question α ἦ ἐθέλεις . . . ; Il. 1.133. Cf. Il. 1.203, Il. 2.229, Il. 5.349, Il. 8.140, Il. 15.18, Il. 19.343, Il. 20.17, etc.: ἦ καί μοι νεμεσήσεαι; Od. 1.158. Cf. Od. 1.391, Od. 3.251, Od. 4.682, Od. 8.336, Od. 9.405, Od. 10.284, Od. 11.160, etc. β In the first clause in questions in disjunctive form (cf. ἠέ 2): ἦ πού τις νήσων ἦε . . . ; Od. 13.234, etc. γ Introducing a question with disjunctive force: ἦ ἀνθρώπων εἰμὶ σχεδόν; Od. 6.125, etc. b Introducing an indirect question: τόδε εἰπέ, ἦ . . . Od. 16.138.
ἦ3. See ἠέ 2.

h)ero/eis.head: ἠερόεις
h)ero/eis.html: ἠερόεις -εντος [ἠερ-, ἀήρ.] 1 Hazy, gloomy, dark: τάρταρον Il. 8.13, ζόφον Il. 12.240, Il. 15.191, Il. 21.56, Il. 23.51: Od. 11.57, 155, Od. 13.241. 2 Hazy, misty: κατʼ ἠερόεντα κέλευθα (through the paths of the clouds) Od. 20.64.

h)ri/on.head: ἠρίον
h)ri/on.html: ἠρίον τό. A grave-mound, a barrow Il. 23.126.

h(/rws.head: ἥρως
h(/rws.html: ἥρως -ωος. Genit. ἥρως Od. 6.303. Dat. ἥρωϊ Il. 9.613, Il. 13.582, Il. 17.137, Il. 23.151, etc.: Od. 2.99, Od. 19.144, Od. 24.134. ἥρῳ Il. 7.453: Od. 8.483. 1 A warrior: στίχας ἡρώων Il. 20.326. Cf. Il. 1.4, Il. 2.483, 579, Il. 16.144 = Il. 19.391, Il. 18.56 = 437, Il. 23.645: Od. 11.329, Od. 21.299. With ἄνδρες: στίχας ἀνδρῶν ἡρώων Il. 5.747 = Il. 8.391. Cf. Il. 9.525, Il. 13.346: Od. 1.101, Od. 4.268, Od. 11.629, Od. 24.25, 88. 2 Prefixed to an ethnic name, of a body of the same race in arms together: ὦ φίλοι ἥρωες Δαναοί Il. 2.110 = Il. 6.67 = Il. 15.733 = Il. 19.78. Cf. Il. 2.256, Il. 12.165, Il. 13.629, Il. 15.219, 230, 261, 702, Il. 19.34, 41: Od. 24.68. 3 Prefixed or added as a sort of title to the name or patronymic of a warrior: ἡ. Ἀτρεΐδης Il. 1.102 = Il. 7.322 = Il. 13.112, Λήϊτος ἡ. Il. 7.35. Cf. Il. 2.708, 844, Il. 4.200, Il. 6.63, Il. 7.453, Il. 9.613, Il. 11.339, 771, Il. 12.95, Il. 13.92, 384, 428, 439, 575, 582, Il. 16.751, 781, Il. 17.137, 706, Il. 18.325, Il. 21.163, Il. 22.298, Il. 23.151, 747, 893, Il. 24.474, 574: Od. 11.520. 4 In voc. as a form of address to a warrior Il. 10.416, Il. 20.104. With a proper name: Εὐρύπυλʼ ἥρως Il. 11.819, 838. 5 Applied to warriors, but signifying little more than the man, the wight: ἔτρεψεν ἀδελφειοῦ φρένας ἡ. Il. 6.61. Cf. Il. 3.377, Il. 7.120 = Il. 13.788, Il. 10.179, Il. 23.824. In apposition: ὅ γʼ ἡ. ἔστη Il. 5.308. Cf. Il. 5.327, Il. 8.268, Il. 10.154, Il. 11.483, Il. 13.164, Il. 23.896. 6 As an honourable appellation of others than warriors: ἐπὶ φᾶρος βάλετʼ ὤμοις ἡ. Od. 15.62. Cf. Od. 7.44, Od. 8.242. With ἄνδρες Od. 14.97. With an ethnic name: ἥρωας Ἀχαιούς Od. 1.272. 7 Prefixed or added as a sort of title to the name or patronymic of another than a warrior: Λαέρτην ἥρωα Od. 1.189. Cf. Od. 2.15, 99 = Od. 19.144 = Od. 24.134, Od. 2.157 = Od. 24.451, Od. 3.415, Od. 4.21 = 303, 617 = Od. 15.117, Od. 6.303, Od. 7.155, Od. 8.483, Od. 11.342, Od. 14.317, Od. 15.52, 121, 131, Od. 18.423, Od. 22.185. 8 In voc. as a form of address to another than a warrior Od. 4.423, Od. 7.303, Od. 10.516. With a proper name: Τηλέμαχʼ ἥρως Od. 4.312.

h)eti/wn.head: Ἠετίων-1
h)eti/wn.html:
Ἠετίων-1 (μεγαλήτωρ). King of Thebe-2 and father of Andromache. His city taken by Achilles and himself slain Il. 1.366, Il. 6.416, Il. 9.188, Il. 16.153; Il. 6.395, 396, Il. 8.187, Il. 22.472, 480, Il. 23.827.
Ἠετίων-2. A Trojan, father of Podes Il. 17.575, 590.
Ἠετίων-3. An Imbrian. Ransomed Lycaon-2 Il. 21.43.

h)=mar.head: ἦμαρ
h)=mar.html: ἦμαρ -ατος, τό [cf. ἡμέρη.] 1 Day, the day, the period of daylight: μέσον ἠ. Il. 21.111, ὄφρʼ ἀέξετο ἠ. Il. 8.66 = Il. 11.84: = Od. 9.56. Cf. Od. 7.288, Od. 10.86, 470, Od. 17.191, Od. 18.367 = Od. 22.301. For δείελον ἠ. see δείελος 2. 2 A day considered as a space of time. a As a period of daylight: πᾶν ἠ. Il. 1.592, νύκτας τε καὶ ἠ. Il. 5.490. Cf. Il. 1.601, Il. 9.326, Il. 18.340, 453, Il. 19.162, Il. 22.432, Il. 23.186, Il. 24.73, 713, 745: Od. 2.345, Od. 5.156, 388, Od. 9.74, 161 = 556 = Od. 10.183 = 476 = Od. 12.29 = Od. 19.424, Od. 10.11, 28, 80 = Od. 15.476, Od. 10.142, Od. 11.183 = Od. 13.338 = Od. 16.39, Od. 16.365, Od. 17.515, Od. 19.513, Od. 20.84, Od. 24.41, 63. b As embracing both daylight and dark: ἐείκοσιν ἤματα Il. 6.217, ἤματα πάντα Il. 8.539 (for ever), Il. 12.133 (ever), Il. 13.826, Il. 14.235 (all my days), 269, 276, Il. 16.499, Il. 23.594, Il. 24.491: Od. 2.205, Od. 4.209, 592, Od. 5.136 = Od. 7.257 = Od. 23.336, Od. 5.210, 219, Od. 6.46, 281, Od. 7.94, Od. 8.431, Od. 9.123, Od. 10.467, Od. 15.54, Od. 21.156, Od. 23.6, Od. 24.25. Cf. Il. 21.45: Od. 4.360, Od. 5.278, Od. 7.267, Od. 19.199. 3 A day considered as a point or unit of time or as one of a series: ἤματι κείνῳ (on that day, that day) Il. 2.37, 482, Il. 4.543, Il. 18.324, Il. 21.517, τρίτῳ ἤματι Il. 11.707, ἤματα πάντα (during or on each day, every day) Il. 19.226. Cf. Il. 2.351, 743, Il. 3.189, Il. 4.164 = Il. 6.448, Il. 5.210, Il. 6.345, 422, Il. 8.475, Il. 9.253 = 439 = Il. 11.766, Il. 9.363, Il. 11.444, Il. 12.279, Il. 13.98, 335, Il. 14.250, Il. 15.76, 252, 719, Il. 16.385, Il. 17.401, Il. 18.85, Il. 19.60, 89, 98, Il. 21.5, 77, 584, Il. 22.359, 471, Il. 23.87: Od. 2.55 = Od. 17.534, Od. 3.180, Od. 5.34, 262, 309, 390 = Od. 9.76 = Od. 10.144, Od. 6.170, Od. 7.326, Od. 8.468, Od. 12.399 = Od. 15.477, Od. 18.137, Od. 19.153 = Od. 24.143, Od. 20.19, 116, Od. 23.252.– ἐπʼ ἤματι Il. 10.48 (in a single day), Il. 19.229 (for the day (and no longer)): Od. 2.284 (in one day), Od. 12.105 (in the day, a day), Od. 14.105 (each day, day by day). Cf. Il. 13.234, Il. 19.110. 4 With an adj., expressing periphrastically the substantival notion implicit in the adj. a αἴσιμον ἠ. (the fatal day, the fate, one's fate) Il. 8.72, Il. 21.100, Il. 22.212: Od. 16.280. b ἠ. ἀναγκαῖον (the day that brings compulsion, slavery) Il. 16.836. c δούλιον ἠ. (the day that brings slavery, slavery) Il. 6.463: Od. 14.340, Od. 17.323. d ἐλεύθερον ἠ. (the day or time of freedom, freedom) Il. 6.455, Il. 16.831, Il. 20.193. e κακὸν ἠ. (the day that brings bane, bane) Il. 9.251, 597, Il. 20.315 = Il. 21.374: Od. 10.269, 288, Od. 15.524. f μόρσιμον ἠ. (the fatal day, one's fate) Il. 15.613: Od. 10.175.– g νηλεὲς ἠ. (the day of pitiless fate, fate, bane) Il. 11.484, 588, Il. 13.514, Il. 15.375, Il. 17.511, 615, Il. 21.57: Od. 8.525, Od. 9.17. h νόστιμον ἠ. (the day that brings one's home-coming, one's home-coming) Od. 1.9, 168, 354, Od. 3.233 = Od. 5.220 = Od. 8.466, Od. 6.311, Od. 16.149, Od. 17.253, 571, Od. 19.369. i ὀλέθριον ἠ. (the day that brings bane, bane) Il. 19.294, 409. j ἠ. ὀρφανικόν (the day that brings orphanhood, orphanhood) Il. 22.490.

h)e/lios.head: ἠέλιος
h)e/lios.html:
ἠέλιος -ου, ὁ. Also Ἥλιος Od. 8.271. Ἠέλιος as voc. Il. 3.277. 1 The sun. a ἅμʼ ἠελίῳ καταδύντι (at sunset) Il. 1.592, ἠ. ἐπέλαμψεν Il. 17.650. Cf. Il. 1.475, Il. 4.44, Il. 5.267, Il. 8.485, 538, Il. 10.547, Il. 14.185, etc.: Od. 2.181, Od. 4.45, Od. 6.98, Od. 7.124, Od. 10.160, Od. 15.404, Od. 20.356, etc. b ὑπʼ αὐγὰς ἠελίοιο, in the upper world, among the livingOd. 11.498, 619, Od. 15.349. Of seeing the sun, i.e. of living: δηρὸν ἔτʼ ὄψεσθαι φάος ἠελίοιο Il. 5.120. Cf. Il. 18.61 = 442, Il. 24.558: Od. 4.540 = Od. 10.498, Od. 4.833, Od. 14.44 = Od. 20.207. Sim. of being born: ἠελίου ἴδεν αὐγάς Il. 16.188. Of leaving the sun, i.e. of dying: λείψειν (λιπὼν) φάος ἠελίοιο Il. 18.11: Od. 11.93. 2 The quarter of the rising sun, the east: πρὸς ἠῶ τʼ ἠέλιόν τε Il. 12.239: Od. 9.26, Od. 13.240. 3 The sun-god: Ἠ. ὃς πάντʼ ἐφορᾷς Il. 3.277. Cf. Il. 3.104, Il. 8.480, Il. 14.344, Il. 19.197, etc.: βοῦς Ὑπερίονος Ἠελίοιο Od. 1.8. Cf. Od. 3.1, Od. 8.271, Od. 10.138, Od. 11.16, 109, Od. 12.133, Od. 19.276, Od. 24.12, etc.
Ἠέλιος Ἥλιος Od. 8.271 (ἀκάμας, παμφανάων , τερψίμβροτος, Ὑπερίων, Ὑπεριονίδης, φαέθων, φαεσίμβροτος). The Sun, father by Perse of Aeetes and Circe Od. 10.138, and by Neaera of Phaethousa and Lampetie Od. 12.132 . Brings to Hephaestus news of his dishonour by Ares Od. 8.271; his oxen Od. 1.8, Od. 12.128 , they are killed by the companions of Odysseus 353. See further in Lexicon.

h(/kw.head: ἥκω
h(/kw.html: ἥκω To have come Il. 5.478: Od. 13.325.

h)maqi/h.head: Ἠμαθίη
h)maqi/h.html: Ἠμαθίη (ἐρατεινή). A district adjoining Pieria Il. 14.226.

h(/bh.head: ἥβη
h(/bh.html:
ἥβη -ης, ἡ. 1 Youthful prime, early manhood: ἥβης μέτρον Il. 11.225, τοῦ περ χαριεστάτη ἥ. (in whom youthful manhood shows most . . .) Il. 24.348. Cf. Il. 13.484, Il. 16.857 = Il. 22.363, Il. 17.25: Od. 4.668, Od. 10.279, Od. 11.317, Od. 18.217, Od. 19.532, Od. 23.212. 2 The vigour or strength proper to this stage of growth: ὄφρʼ ἥβῃ πεποίθεα Od. 8.181. Cf. Il. 23.432. In reference to an elderly man, bodily vigour, suppleness of frame: οὐδέ τι ἥβης δεύεται Od. 8.136, δέμας ὤφελλε καὶ ἥβην Od. 16.174 (in both cases of Odysseus). 3 Manhood viewed as a stage attained or to be attained: ἥβην ἵξεσθαι Il. 24.728. Cf. Od. 15.366.
Ἥβη (καλλίσφυρος, πότνια ). Daughter of Zeus and Hera. Acts as cup-bearer to the gods Il. 4.2; helps Hera to prepare a chariot Il. 5.722; tends Ares when cured of his wound Il. 5.905: Heracles her husband Od. 11.603.

h)=noy.head: ἦνοψ
h)=noy.html:
ἦνοψ -οπος. Of unknown meaning. Perh. glittering, gleaming, or the like: ἤνοπι χαλκῷ Il. 16.408, Il. 18.349: = Od. 10.360.
Ἦνοψ-1. Father of Satnius by a naiad Il. 14.445; and father also of Thestor Il. 16.401.
Ἦνοψ-2. Father of Clytomedes Il. 23.634.

h(/faistos.head: Ἥφαιστος
h(/faistos.html:
Ἥφαιστος [use of the proper name.] A fire: σπλάγχνʼ ὑπείρεχον Ἡφαίστοιο Il. 2.426.
Ἥφαιστος (ἀμφιγυήεις, ἄναξ , κλυτοεργός, κλυτοτέχνης , κυλλοποδίων, περικλυτός , πολύμητις, πολύφρων , χαλκεύς). Son of Zeus and Hera. Husband in Il. (Il. 18.382) of Charis, in Od. (Od. 8.267) of Aphrodite . His lameness Il. 18.394, Il. 20.36, etc. : Od. 8.308, etc. His craftsmanship Il. 1.607, Il. 14.166, Il. 18.417, 468, etc.: Od. 8.272, etc. Persuades his mother to conciliate Zeus Il. 1.571; his fall from Olympus Il. 1.590; made Agamemnon's sceptre Il. 2.101, and the breastplate of Diomedes Il. 8.195, and the aegis Il. 15.310; Thetis goes to beg him for armour for her son Il. 18.369, which he makes 468 ; he tells how Eurynome-1 and Thetis tended him when rejected by Hera Il. 18.394; Hera summons him to quell Xanthus-1 Il. 21.330 ; etc. : Od. 4.617, Od. 6.233 , Od. 7.92; Demodocus tells how Ares and Aphrodite deceived him and how he punished them Od. 8.266 , 270, 286, 287, 293, 297, 327, 330, 345, 355, 359; Od. 15.117, Od. 23.160, Od. 24.71, 75. See also in Lex.

h)lw/nh.head: Ἠλώνη
h)lw/nh.html: Ἠλώνη A town of Thessaly. Its men led by Polypoetes and Leonteus Il. 2.739.

h)mu/w.head: ἠμύω
h)mu/w.html: ἠμύω (ὑπεμνήμυκε.) 1 To cause to bend, bow, droop: κάρη Il. 8.308. 2 To bend, bow, droop: λήϊον ἠμύει ἀσταχύεσσιν (with its ears) Il. 2.148, ἤμυσε καρήατι Il. 19.405. Of a city nodding or tottering to its fall Il. 2.373 = Il. 4.290.

h(nioxeu/s.head: ἡνιοχεύς
h(nioxeu/s.html: ἡνιοχεύς ὁ. 1 = ἡνίοχος 1 Il. 5.505, Il. 8.312, Il. 16.737. 2 Used loosely of the παραιβάτης (cf. ἡνίοχος 2) Il. 19.401.

h(=par.head: ἧπαρ
h(=par.html: ἧπαρ -ατος, τό. The liver Il. 11.579 = Il. 13.412 = Il. 17.349, Il. 20.469, 470, Il. 24.212: Od. 9.301, Od. 11.578, Od. 22.83.

h)nemo/eis.head: ἠνεμόεις
h)nemo/eis.html: ἠνεμόεις -εσσα [ἄνεμος.] Blown upon or vexed by the winds: ἄκριας Od. 9.400, Od. 16.365. Cf. Il. 22.145: Od. 19.432. Epithet of places. Of Troy Il. 3.305, Il. 8.499 = Il. 12.115, Il. 13.724, Il. 18.174, Il. 23.64, 297. Of Enispe Il. 2.606. Of Mimas Od. 3.172.

h)=ri.head: ἦρι
h)=ri.html: ἦρι [ἀϝερ-. See ἠέριος.] Early in the morning Il. 9.360: Od. 19.320, Od. 20.156.

h)/kestos.head: ἤκεστος
h)/kestos.html: ἤκεστος -η [doubtfully explained as fr. ἠ- = ἀ-1 + -κεστος. See κεστός.] Thus, untouched by the goad: βοῦς ἠκέστας Il. 6.94 = 275, 309.

h)peropeu/w.head: ἠπεροπεύω
h)peropeu/w.html: ἠπεροπεύω 1 To deceive, cozen: ἵνʼ ἐμὰς φρένας ἠπεροπεύσῃς Od. 13.327. Absol. Od. 14.400. To trick, take unfair advantage of Il. 23.605. 2 To beguile the heart of, lead astray (a woman) Il. 5.349: Od. 15.419. So τάτε φρένας ἠπεροπεύει γυναιξίν Od. 15.421. With direct and cognate acc.: τί με ταῦτα λιλαίεαι ἠπεροπεύειν; (to beguile me thus) Il. 3.399.

h)e/.head: ἠέ
h)e/.html: ἠέ (ἠϝέ), ἤ. 1 Disjunctive particle. a Or: ἐγὼ ἢ ἄλλος Ἀχαιῶν Il. 2.231. Cf. Il. 1.40, 515, Il. 2.800, Il. 3.394, Il. 4.83, 142, etc.: εἰλαπίνη ἠὲ γάμος; Od. 1.226. Cf. Od. 1.162, 282, Od. 2.375, Od. 3.94, Od. 4.45, 396, etc. So ἤ τε (ἤτε) Il. 19.148. b ἠὲ (ἢ) . . . ἠὲ (ἢ) . . ., either . . . or . . .: ἢ νῦν δηθύνοντʼ ἢ ὕστερον αὖτις ἰόντα Il. 1.27. Cf. Il. 1.138, 395, Il. 5.484, Il. 9.78, 537, Il. 10.370, etc.: ἠὲ δόλῳ ἢ ἀμφαδόν Od. 1.296. Cf. Od. 3.99, 217, Od. 4.546, Od. 5.484, Od. 6.103, Od. 10.228, etc. Thrice or four times Il. 1.145, Il. 7.179, Il. 10.6, etc.: Od. 10.433, Od. 15.84, etc. So ἤ τε (ἤτε) . . . ἤ τε (ἤτε) . . . Il. 9.276 = Il. 19.177, Il. 11.410, Il. 17.42.– ἢ . . . τε Il. 2.289. 2 In questions in disjunctive form (the second particle written ἦε, ἦ). a Direct: ἠέ τι βέβληαι, ἦε . . .; Il. 13.251. Cf. Il. 15.735, etc.: Od. 3.72, Od. 24.109, etc. Thrice Il. 13.308, etc. Without the particle in the first clause Il. 15.203, etc.: Od. 20.130, Od. 21.194, etc. b Indirect, whether . . . or . . .: μερμήριξεν, ἢ . . . ἦε . . . Il. 1.190. Cf. Il. 2.238, Il. 4.15, Il. 5.86, Il. 8.377, Il. 13.327, Il. 18.308 (and see whether . . .), etc.: ὄφρʼ ἐῢ εἰδῶ, ἠὲ . . . ἦ . . . Od. 1.175. Cf. Od. 1.268, Od. 3.170, Od. 4.28, Od. 6.142, Od. 11.175, Od. 16.260, Od. 19.525, etc. Without the particle in the first clause Il. 10.546, etc.: Od. 4.837, etc. With εἰ or αἴ in the first clause Il. 2.368, Il. 6.368, Il. 8.533, Il. 22.246: Od. 24.218. With change of construction Od. 17.275. 3 After comparatives, than: ἀρείοσιν ἠέ περ ὑμῖν Il. 1.260. Cf. Il. 5.531, Il. 8.190, Il. 16.688, etc.: νεώτεροι ἢ πάρος ἦσαν Od. 10.395. Cf. Od. 1.322, Od. 8.154, etc. So ἤ τε (ἤτε) Od. 16.216. After ἄλλος Il. 10.404, etc. After ἀλλοῖος Od. 16.181, Od. 19.267. After verbs implying comparison: βούλομαι . . . ἢ . . . Il. 1.117, etc.: ἔφθης . . . ἢ . . . Od. 11.58, etc.

h)=mos.head: ἦμος
h)=mos.html: ἦμος When, at the time when. 1 With indic.: ἦμος δʼ ἠέλιος κατέδυ Il. 1.475. Cf. Il. 1.477, Il. 16.779, etc.: Od. 2.1, Od. 9.58, 168, etc. Introducing a simile Od. 12.439. Correlative with τῆμος. See τῆμος 2. 2 With subj. in a conditional relative sentence. See Table at end III.B.a 1.

h)/dh.head: ἤδη
h)/dh.html: ἤδη [ἦ2 δή.] 1 Previously to some specified or indicated time, by or before this (or that) time, by now, now, already, ere this: ἤδη οἱ ἐφῆκα βέλος Il. 5.188. Cf. Il. 1.250, 260, 590, Il. 2.699, Il. 3.56, 184, etc.: ἤδη Ἄϊδόσδε βεβήκει Od. 3.410. Cf. Od. 2.164, 211, 402, 410, Od. 3.241, 335, etc. Reinforcing νῦν Il. 15.110, etc.: Od. 14.213, etc. 2 In reference to the future, now: ἧ ἤδη με δαμόωσιν Il. 6.368. Cf. Il. 11.821, Il. 16.438, Il. 23.20, Il. 24.635, etc.: ἤδη σχεθέτω φόρμιγγα Od. 8.537. Cf. Od. 1.303, Od. 4.294, Od. 13.151, Od. 19.300, Od. 22.101, Od. 24.506, etc. Reinforcing νῦν Il. 1.456, etc.: Od. 10.472, etc.

h)=dos.head: ἦδος
h)=dos.html: ἦδος τό [cf. ἡδύς.] Pleasure, profit, satisfaction: μίνυνθα ἡμέων ἔσσεται ἠ. (we shall profit our friends little) Il. 11.318, τί μοι τῶν ἠ.; (what satisfaction have I in that ?) Il. 18.80. Cf. Il. 1.576: = Od. 18.404, Od. 24.95.

h)baio/s.head: ἠβαιός
h)baio/s.html: ἠβαιός -ή, -όν. 1 Little, inconsiderable, of small worth, few in number: οὔ οἱ ἔνι τρίχες οὐδʼ ἠβαιαί Od. 18.355. Cf. Il. 14.141: Od. 21.288. 2 Absol. in neut. sing. ἠβαιόν a A little space, a short distance: ἐλθόντες ἠ. ἀπὸ σπείους Od. 9.462. Cf. Il. 13.702. b For a short space of time, for a little: οὐκ ἀνάβλησις ἔσσεται οὐδʼ ἠ. Il. 2.380. Cf. Il. 2.386, Il. 13.106. c A little, to a small or trifling extent: οὔ σε χρὴ αἰδοῦς οὐδʼ ἠ. Od. 3.14. Cf. Il. 20.361.

h)pio/dwros.head: ἠπιόδωρος
h)pio/dwros.html: ἠπιόδωρος -ον [ἤπιος + δῶρον.] App., generous in giving, bountiful in supplying her children's needs, grudging them nothing: μήτηρ Il. 6.251.

h)/liqa.head: ἤλιθα
h)/liqa.html: ἤλιθα [poss. conn. with ἅλις.] Strengthening πολλός: ἤλιθα πολλήν Il. 11.677. Cf. Od. 5.483, Od. 9.330, Od. 14.215, Od. 19.443.

h(mi/onos.head: ἡμίονος
h(mi/onos.html: ἡμίονος -ου, ὁ, ἡ [ἡμι- + ὄνος. A half-ass.] 1 A mule (doubtless including the hinny) Il. 7.333, Il. 10.352, Il. 17.742, Il. 23.121, Il. 24.150, etc.: Od. 4.636, Od. 6.37, Od. 7.2, Od. 8.124, Od. 15.85, Od. 17.298, etc. In Il. 2.852 (ἡμιόνων ἀγροτεράων) app. not strictly mules but some species intermediate between the horse and the ass. 2 Like ἵππος 3: ἐφʼ ἡμιόνων κείμενον (i.e. on the waggon) Il. 24.702.

h)=nis.head: ἦνις
h)=nis.html: ἦνις [doubtfully explained as fr. ἔνος, cited in sense year.] Thus, one year old, that is a yearling: δυοκαίδεκα βοῦς ἤνις Il. 6.94 = 275, 309, βοῦν ἦνιν Il. 10.292: = Od. 3.382.

h)/ia.head: ἤϊα1
h)/ia.html: ἤϊα1, τά. Contr. ᾖα Od. 5.266, Od. 9.212. 1 Provisions for a voyage: ὅπλισσον ἤϊα Od. 2.289, ἤϊα φερώμεθα 410, ἤῗά κε πάντα κατέφθιτο Od. 4.363, ἐν καὶ ᾖα κωρύκῳ Od. 5.266, Od. 9.212, νηὸς ἐξέφθιτο ἤῗα πάντα Od. 12.329. 2 Prey: θώων ἤϊα πέλονται Il. 13.103. 3 Chaff (in this sense perh. a different word): ὡς ἄνεμος ζαὴς ἠΐων (disyllable) θημῶνα τινάξῃ Od. 5.368.

h)ere/qomai.head: ἠερέθομαι
h)ere/qomai.html: ἠερέθομαι [ἀείρομαι. Cf. ἠγερέθομαι beside ἀγείρομαι.] 1 To take wing: ὡς ἀκρίδες ἠερέθονται Il. 21.12. 2 To wave about, flutter: θύσανοι ἠερέθονται Il. 2.448. Fig., of the mind, to be blown about by passion or caprice, to be unsteady or untrustworthy Il. 3.108.

h)le/ktwr.head: ἠλέκτωρ
h)le/ktwr.html: ἠλέκτωρ The sun Il. 6.513, Il. 19.398.

h(mio/neios.head: ἡμιόνειος
h(mio/neios.html: ἡμιόνειος -η, -ον [ἡμίονος.] 1 Drawn by mules Il. 24.189, 266: Od. 6.72. 2 For, worn by, mules Il. 24.268.

h)pu/ta.head: ἠπύτα
h)pu/ta.html: ἠπύτα (ᾰ) [ἠπύω. Prob. orig. a voc. turned into a nom.]. Loud-voiced: κῆρυξ Il. 7.384.

h)xh/eis.head: ἠχήεις
h)xh/eis.html: ἠχήεις -εσσα (ϝηχήεις) [(ϝ)ηχή.] Sounding. Epithet of the sea Il. 1.157. Of a house, echoing Od. 4.72.

h(rakle/hs.head: Ἡρακλέης
h(rakle/hs.html: Ἡρακλέης Ἡρακλῆς (θεῖος, θρασυμέμνων θυμολέων, κρατερός, κρατερόφρων, μεγάλων ἐπιίστωρ ἔργων , μένος αἰὲν ἀτειρής). Son of Alcmene by Zeus (nominally by Amphitryon) Il. 14.324 : Od. 11.267. Father of Tlepolemus-1 by Astyocheia Il. 2.658 , 666; father also of Thessalus Il. 2.679: husband of Hebe Od. 11.603. His birth delayed by contrivance of Hera, whereby he became subject to Eurystheus Il. 19.95, Il. 15.640; wounded Hera with an arrow Il. 5.392; being wronged by Laomedon sacked Troy Il. 5.638, his return thence hindered by Hera Il. 14.249, 266, Il. 15.25; carried off the dog of Hades Il. 8.366: Od. 11.623; vexed Pylus Il. 11.690 ; the wall built for him against the sea monster Il. 20.145 ; his fate Il. 18.117: Od. 8.224 ; his phantom in the Shades Od. 11.601; killed Iphitus-2 Od. 21.26.

h)qei=os.head: ἠθεῖος
h)qei=os.html: ἠθεῖος -η. In voc. ἠθεῖε as a form of address to an elder or a master Il. 6.518 (Paris to Hector), Il. 10.37 (Menelaus to Agamemnon), Il. 22.229, 239 (the supposed Deïphobus to Hector). Sim. in the periphrasis ἠθείη κεφαλή Il. 23.94 (Achilles to the shade of Patroclus. Patroclus was the senior Il. 11.787). In Od. 14.147 (ἠθεῖόν μιν καλέω) Eumaeus means that he mentally addresses his absent master as ἠθεῖε.

h)ma/tios.head: ἠμάτιος
h)ma/tios.html: ἠμάτιος -η [ἠματ-, ἦμαρ.] 1 By day, in the day-time: ἠματίη ὑφαίνεσκεν Od. 2.104 = Od. 24.139. Cf. Od. 19.149. 2 Day by day, daily Il. 9.72.

h(ge/omai.head: ἡγέομαι
h(ge/omai.html: ἡγέομαι Fut. ἡγήσομαι Il. 14.374. 3 sing. aor. ἡγήσατο Il. 1.71, Il. 2.867, Il. 12.251, Il. 20.144, etc.: Od. 2.405, Od. 5.192, Od. 14.48, Od. 24.469, etc. 3 dual -άσθην Il. 2.620, 678, 864, 870. Subj. ἡγήσομαι Od. 15.82. 2 sing. opt. ἡγήσαιο Od. 7.22. 3 sing. -αιτο Il. 2.687: Od. 6.114, 300. 3 sing. imp. ἡγησάσθω Il. 9.168. Infin. ἡγήσασθαι Il. 22.101: Od. 10.263, Od. 14.238. (ἐξ-.) 1 To act as guide or pilot, show the way: καὶ ἂν πάϊς ἡγήσαιτο Od. 6.300. Cf. Od. 13.65, Od. 15.82. With dat., to guide (a person), show (him) the way: ἥ οἱ πόλιν ἡγήσαιτο (to the city) Od. 6.114. Cf. Il. 1.71: Od. 7.22. With cognate acc., to show (the way): τὸν ἠνώγεα αὐτὴν ὁδὸν ἡγήσασθαι (to take me by the way by which he had come) Od. 10.263. 2 To lead the way, act as leader, take the lead: ὣς φωνήσας ἡγήσατο Il. 20.144. Cf. Il. 9.168, 192, Il. 12.28, Il. 24.96: Od. 1.125, Od. 2.405 = Od. 3.29 = Od. 7.37, Od. 2.413 = Od. 8.46 = 104, Od. 5.192, Od. 14.48. 3 To lead the way, give a lead, in a course of action. With dat.: τοῖσιν εὐπείθης ἡγήσατο νηπιέῃσιν (in their . . .) Od. 24.469. To give a lead, cause a start to be made. With dat. and genit. of that in which a start is made: ἀοιδὸς ἡμῖν ἡγείσθω ὀρχηθμοῖο Od. 23.134. 4 To be the leader, commander or chief of. a With genit.: ἐπικούρων Il. 12.101. Cf. Il. 2.567, 620, 638, 678, 731, 851, 867, 870. b With dat.: Μῄοσιν Il. 2.864, νῆες, ᾗσιν Ἀχιλλεὺς ἐς Τροίην ἡγεῖτο (brought to Troy under his command) Il. 16.169. Cf. Il. 2.687, Il. 5.211: Od. 14.238. 5 Absol., to act as chief or leader, lead one's men Il. 12.251 = Il. 13.833, Il. 13.802, Il. 14.374: Od. 14.470. To lead a person on, induce him to follow: κερδοσύνῃ ἡγήσατο Il. 22.247. 6 To lead or lead on (one's men). With genit.: ἡγήσατο λαῶν Il. 15.311. With dat.: Τρωσὶ ποτὶ πτόλιν ἡγήσασθαι Il. 22.101. 7 To take the lead, be the leading person, among. With dat.: ἡγεῖτο μνηστῆρσιν Od. 16.397.

h)w=qen.head: ἠῶθεν
h)w=qen.html: ἠῶθεν [ἠώς + -θεν 1.] From the dawn; hence, at dawn, in the morning. Referring to the next morning: ἠ. ἴτω ἐπὶ νῆας Il. 7.372. Cf. Il. 7.381, Il. 11.555 = Il. 17.664, Il. 18.136, Il. 23.49, Il. 24.401: ἠ. ἀγορήνδε καθεζώμεσθα κιὁντες Od. 1.372. Cf. Od. 3.153, 366, Od. 4.214, Od. 7.189, Od. 12.293, Od. 14.512, Od. 15.308, 506, Od. 17.600, Od. 18.248, Od. 19.320, Od. 21.265, 280, Od. 24.72.

h)la/skw.head: ἠλάσκω
h)la/skw.html: ἠλάσκω [ἄλη.] To rove or flit about: ἔλαφοι καθʼ ὕλην αὔτως ἠλάσκουσαι Il. 13.104. Cf. Il. 2.470.

h)nore/h.head: ἠνορέη
h)nore/h.html: ἠνορέη -ης, ἡ [ἀνήρ.] Instrumental ἠνορέηφι Il. 4.303. Manliness, valour, mettle, prowess: ἠνορέηφι πεποιθώς Il. 4.303. Cf. Il. 6.156, Il. 8.226 = Il. 11.9, Il. 17.329: Od. 24.509.

h)=lis.head: Ἦλις
h)=lis.html: Ἦλις (δῖα, εὐρύχορος, ἱππόβοτος). A town and country in the north west extremity of the Peloponnesus Il. 2.615, 626, Il. 11.673, 686, 698: Od. 4.635, Od. 13.275, Od. 15.298, Od. 21.347, Od. 24.431.

h)u/te.head: ἠΰτε
h)u/te.html: ἠΰτε [cf. εὖτε.] 1 As when, introducing similes. With indic. Il. 2.87, 455, 480, Il. 3.3, Il. 16.487, Il. 21.573, Il. 22.139. With subj. Il. 17.547. Without expressed vb. Il. 2.469, Il. 15.618, Il. 17.737: Od. 21.48. 2 Like, as: ἠΰτʼ ὀμίχλη Il. 1.359. Cf. Il. 2.754, Il. 4.243, Il. 7.219, Il. 19.374, etc.: Od. 8.280, 518, Od. 11.222, Od. 17.463, etc. 3 After a comp., than: μελάντερον ἠΰτε πίσσα Il. 4.277.

h)/kistos.head: ἤκιστος
h)/kistos.html: ἤκιστος [superl. fr. ἦκα. Cf. ἥσσων.] The slowest or weakest: ἠ. ἐλαυνέμεν (in driving) Il. 23.531.

h(me/rh.head: ἡμέρη
h(me/rh.html: ἡμέρη -ης, ἡ [cf. ἦμαρ.] = ἦμαρ 3: ἡ. ἥδε Il. 8.541 = Il. 13.828. Cf. Od. 11.294 = Od. 14.293, Od. 14.93, Od. 24.514.

h(=lic.head: ἧλιξ
h(=lic.html: ἧλιξ -ικος. Of the same age: βόες Od. 18.373.

h)la/kata.head: ἠλάκατα
h)la/kata.html: ἠλάκατα τά [ἠλακάτη.] The yarn spun off from the distaff Od. 6.53, 306, Od. 7.105, Od. 17.97, Od. 18.315.

h)/peiro/nde.head: ἤπειρόνδε
h)/peiro/nde.html: ἤπειρόνδε [acc. of ἤπειρος. + -δε 1.] 1 To or on to the land as opposed to the sea: ἐκ πόντου βὰς ἠ. Od. 5.56. Cf. Od. 5.438, Od. 9.73, 485, Od. 10.403, 423, Od. 13.116, Od. 23.236. 2 To the mainland as opposed to an island: πέμψω σʼ ἠ. Od. 18.84, ἀνάξομέν μιν ἠ. 115 (in both cases said in Ithaca).

h)lu/sios.head: Ἠλύσιος
h)lu/sios.html: Ἠλύσιος [said to be for ἠλύθ-τιος, fr. ἠλυθ- (see ἔρχομαι). To which . . . go.] Ἠλύσιον πεδίον, an abode of everlasting bliss assigned to mortals favoured by the godsOd. 4.563.

h)peropeu/s.head: ἠπεροπεύς
h)peropeu/s.html: ἠπεροπεύς ὁ [ἠπεροπεύω.] A cheat, deceiver, cozener, beguiler: ἠπεροπῆά τε καὶ ἐπίκλοπον Od. 11.364.

h(ni/ka.head: ἡνίκα
h(ni/ka.html: ἡνίκα When: ἡ. ἀγινεῖς αἶγας Od. 22.198.

h)/lektron.head: ἤλεκτρον
h)/lektron.html: ἤλεκτρον τό. 1 Amber Od. 4.73. 2 In pl., beads of amber: ὅρμον ἠλέκτροισιν ἐερμένον Od. 18.296. Cf. Od. 15.460.

h(meri/s.head: ἡμερίς
h(meri/s.html: ἡμερίς ἡ [ἥμερος. Cf. κραταιός, κραταιΐς.] The cultivated vine, the vine Od. 5.69.

h(du/potos.head: ἡδύποτος
h(du/potos.html: ἡδύποτος [ἡδύς + πο-, πίνω.] Sweet to drink. Of wine Od. 2.340, Od. 3.391, Od. 15.507.

h(ghla/zw.head: ἡγηλάζω
h(ghla/zw.html: ἡγηλάζω [*ἡγηλός, apt to lead, fr. ἡγέομαι.] 1 To play the leader or fugleman to: κακὸς κακὸν ἡγηλάζει Od. 17.217. 2 To lead (a specified kind of existence), endure (a specified fate): κακὸν μόρον ἡγηλάζεις Od. 11.618.

h)oi=os.head: ἠοῖος
h)oi=os.html: ἠοῖος -η, -ον [ἠώς.] 1 Of the east, dwelling in the east, eastern Od. 8.29. 2 In fem. as sb., the morning: πᾶσαν ἠοίην μένομεν Od. 4.447.
